title: 🏛️ Exam 2024 · writing prepared: the doctor's advice ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Last week, your health club welcomed Doctor James to advise the students to keep fit and healthy. The exam asks for a 5-sentence e-mail to your cousin. What must the e-mail tell your cousin?

options.text: what Doctor James advised the students to do
what you did in the club last week with your friends
what you like to eat at the weekend with your family
what your cousin should do for his or her birthday party

questions.explanation: The task is about the advice that the doctor gave to the students, so the e-mail tells that advice to the cousin. The exam says advised you to; to keep the sentences correct, the e-mail here gives the advice in direct style, with You should and You must. What you did in the club, what you eat or the cousin's birthday are true subjects, but they are not what the task asks.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) You prepare the advice for your e-mail. Which pieces of advice fit a doctor's talk about keeping fit and healthy? Select ALL that fit.

options.text: You should eat fruit and vegetables every day.
You should sleep at three in the morning.
You should drink lots of water.
You should eat sweets before every meal.
You should sleep nine hours every night.
You should eat crisps for breakfast.

questions.explanation: A doctor who talks about keeping fit advises eating fruit and vegetables, drinking water and sleeping well. Sleeping at three in the morning, eating sweets before every meal and eating crisps for breakfast are the opposite of a healthy life, so they do not belong to this advice.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) The e-mail goes from Fadi(a) to his or her cousin Sami(a). The exam frame needs an opening and a closing. Which pair is right?

options.text: Dear Fadi(a), ... Yours, Sami(a)
Dear Sami(a), ... Yours, Fadi(a)
Dear Sami(a), ... Yours, Sami(a)
Dear Fadi(a), ... Yours, Fadi(a)

questions.explanation: The opening names the person who reads the e-mail, the cousin, and the closing carries the name of the person who writes it. Every other pair gives the same name twice or swaps the writer and the reader.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Fadi(a) writes the five sentences of the e-mail. Which sentence belongs in an e-mail about Doctor James's advice?

options.text: My brother has a new bike for his birthday.
Doctor James says we should drink lots of water.
I like the colour of the walls of our club.
Last summer I went to the sea with my cousin Ali.

questions.explanation: Every sentence of the paragraph must support the topic, which is the doctor's advice. The sentence about the water gives a piece of advice, while the new bike, the colour of the walls and last summer are true sentences that have nothing to do with keeping fit.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Fadi(a) plans the e-mail to the cousin in four steps. Put the steps in the right order.

options.text: Give Doctor James's advice with You should and You must
Close the e-mail with your name
Greet your cousin in the opening line
Say that Doctor James visited your health club last week

questions.explanation: A message starts with the opening line that greets the reader and ends with the closing line that carries the writer's name. Between them, the writer first says who visited the club and when, and only then gives the advice that the visit brought.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) In his talk, Doctor James gives a good idea: walking to school every day. It is up to each student to follow it. How do you write this advice in your e-mail?

options.text: You should walk to school every day.
You must walk to school every day.
You should to walk to school every day.
You shoulds walk to school every day.

questions.explanation: A good idea that nobody has to follow is advice, and advice is given with should + bare verb: You should walk to school every day. The word must would make it a rule, should to adds a to that a modal never takes, and shoulds adds an -s to a modal, which never changes.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) The club has a rule that Doctor James repeats to everybody: wash your hands before a meal. Which sentence of your e-mail states this rule?

options.text: You should wash your hands before you eat.
You must to wash your hands before you eat.
You musts wash your hands before you eat.
You must wash your hands before you eat.

questions.explanation: A rule that everybody has to follow is stated with must + bare verb: You must wash your hands before you eat. The word should would only give a good idea, must to adds a to, and musts adds an -s to a modal, which never changes.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Doctor James warns about screens: watching TV late at night is a bad idea, although nothing is forbidden. How do you write it in your e-mail?

options.text: You mustn't watch TV late at night.
You shouldn't watching TV late at night.
You shouldn't watch TV late at night.
You don't should watch TV late at night.

questions.explanation: A bad idea that is not forbidden is given with shouldn't + bare verb: You shouldn't watch TV late at night. The word mustn't would make it forbidden, shouldn't eating adds -ing to the verb after a modal, and don't should puts a do before a modal, which never takes one.
